output.brief: The rejections trace to a data-entry error in your own systems, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra fruit or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation suite, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record and kept its 7.0°C carriage temperature. Your specification is 4.0°C. Every Meridane container since go-live was sent at 7.0°C and the carrier held it there, and all five were rejected. Every container carried at 4.0°C passed, including ones packed with the new fungicide. That rules out the fungicide and the Meridane equipment fault. Transit time doesn't explain it either, since the passing and failing containers had overlapping transit times. Lower Serra pallets did worse inside the rejected containers, but that is only an association, because the passing containers weren't surveyed. Don't suspend growers, don't file the refrigeration claim, and don't switch fungicide on this basis. Next: correct the temperature on the mandarin record today. Have Meridane reset the container at sea (sailed 3 Oct) and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4.0°C. Add a check of reefer settings against the product specification before each booking is sent. Review the other products copied into the new system for the same fault. Confidence is high.
